<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:lti-sde-kernel}
A function $k\colon \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ is an \emph{LTI-SDE-induced kernel} if it is the matrix-valued covariance function of a stochastic process $\mathbf{y}(t)$ admitting a state-space representation of the form \cite{sarkka:sde,hartikainen2010a}
\begin{subequations}\label{eq:sde}
	\begin{align}
	\label{eq:sde:state}
		\frac{\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} \mathbf{x}(t)}{\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t} & =\mathbf{F}\mathbf{x}(t)+\mathbf{G}\mathbf{w}(t), \\
		\mathbf{y}(t)                   & =\mathbf{C}(t)\mathbf{x}(t),
	\end{align}
\end{subequations}
where $\mathbf{F}\in \mathbb{R}^{p\times p}$, $\mathbf{G}\in \mathbb{R}^{p\times r}$, and $\mathbf{C}(t)\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times p}$. Here, $\mathbf{w}(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{r}$ denotes zero-mean Gaussian white noise, i.e., the formal derivative of a Brownian motion with diffusion matrix $\mathbf{Q}_{\mathbf{w}} \in \mathbb{R}^{r\times r}$, so that $\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{w}(t)\mathbf{w}(t')^\top] = \mathbf{Q}_{\mathbf{w}}\,\delta(t-t')$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
The state equation in \eqref{eq:sde:state} is understood as shorthand for the corresponding Itô SDE
	\begin{align*}
	\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} \mathbf{x}(t) & = \mathbf{F}\mathbf{x}(t)\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} t + \mathbf{G} \mathbf{Q}_{\mathbf{w}}^{1/2} \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} \mathbf{W}(t),
\end{align*}
where $\mathbf{W}(t)$ is a standard $r$-dimensional Brownian motion. The process $\mathbf{y}(t)$ is then a zero-mean Gaussian process with kernel function $k$.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
We demonstrate the resulting framework on LTI-SDE-induced kernels, including
	      Matérn, spline, celerite, DC, TC, and stable spline kernels.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:sde-to-sss}
    Let $\mathbf{y}(t)$ be a zero-mean Gaussian process defined by the LTI SDE model in \eqref{eq:sde} with kernel function $k(t,t') = \operatorname{cov}(\mathbf{y}(t),\mathbf{y}(t'))$. For any nondecreasing sequence $(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$, the covariance matrix $\mathbf{K}$ with blocks $\mathbf{K}_{ij} = k(t_i,t_j)$ admits an SSS representation of the form \eqref{eq:sss:symmetric} with generators
    \begin{align}\label{eq:sss:generators:nonstationary}

        \mathbf{U}_i & = \mathbf{C}(t_i), &
        \mathbf{T}_i & = \ensuremath{\mathrm{e}}^{\mathbf{F} \Delta t_{i}}, &
        \mathbf{V}_i & = \mathbf{C}(t_i) \mathbf{P}(t_i) \mathbf{T}_i^{\top}, &
        \mathbf{D}_i & = \mathbf{C}(t_i) \mathbf{P}(t_i) \mathbf{C}(t_i)^\top, & i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}.
    
\end{align}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The SSS representation of $\mathbf{K}$ follows directly from \eqref{eq:sde:nonstationary:cov} and the definition of the chain product in \eqref{eq:chain:product}, which implies that for any $\tau \in [t',t]$, we have $\ensuremath{\mathrm{e}}^{\mathbf{F}(t-t')} = \ensuremath{\mathrm{e}}^{\mathbf{F} (t-\tau)}\ensuremath{\mathrm{e}}^{\mathbf{F}(\tau - t')}$. Using this property, we find that for $i>j$,
\begin{align*}
  k(t_i,t_j) &= \mathbf{C}(t_i)\ensuremath{\mathrm{e}}^{\mathbf{F} (t_i-t_j)} \mathbf{P}(t_j)\mathbf{C}(t_j)^\top\\
  &= \mathbf{C}(t_i)\ensuremath{\mathrm{e}}^{\mathbf{F} \Delta t_{i-1}}\cdots \ensuremath{\mathrm{e}}^{\mathbf{F} \Delta t_{j+1}} \ensuremath{\mathrm{e}}^{\mathbf{F} \Delta t_{j}}\mathbf{P}(t_j)\mathbf{C}(t_j)^\top\\
  &= \mathbf{C}(t_i)\mathbf{T}_{i-1:j+1} \mathbf{T}_j\mathbf{P}(t_j)\mathbf{C}(t_j)^\top.
  \end{align*}
  Comparing with \eqref{eq:sss:symmetric}, we see that $\mathbf{K}_{ij} = \mathbf{U}_i\mathbf{T}_{i-1:j+1}\mathbf{V}_j^\top$ for $i>j$. The cases $i=j$ and $i<j$ follow similarly.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
An analogous result holds when the sequence $(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$ is nonincreasing. Indeed, if $\mathbf{K}$ has the form \eqref{eq:sss:symmetric} and $\mathbf{J}_n$ is the exchange (reversal) matrix of order $n$, then the symmetric block permutation $(\mathbf{J}_n \otimes \mathbf{I}_d)\mathbf{K}(\mathbf{J}_n \otimes \mathbf{I}_d)$ preserves the SSS structure: $(\mathbf{J}_n \otimes \mathbf{I}_d)\mathbf{K}(\mathbf{J}_n \otimes \mathbf{I}_d)$ is again symmetric and SSS with the representation
\[ (\mathbf{J}_n \otimes \mathbf{I}_d) \mathbf{K} (\mathbf{J}_n \otimes \mathbf{I}_d) = \hat{\mathbf{V}}(\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{N}^p\hat{\mathbf{T}}^\top)^{-1}\mathbf{N}^p\hat{\mathbf{U}}^\top + \hat{\mathbf{U}}(\mathbf{N}^\top)^p(\mathbf{I} -\mathbf{N}^p\hat{\mathbf{T}}^\top)^{-\top}\hat{\mathbf{V}}^\top
+  \hat{\mathbf{D}}, \]
where $\hat{\mathbf{U}}$, $\hat{\mathbf{T}}$, $\hat{\mathbf{V}}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{D}}$ denote the block diagonal matrices obtained from $\mathbf{U}$, $\mathbf{T}$, $\mathbf{V}$, and $\mathbf{D}$ by reversing the order of the blocks.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
We note that while the time warp $\phi(t)=e^{-\alpha t}$ is monotone, it maps a nondecreasing sequence of time points $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ to a nonincreasing sequence of time points $\phi(t_1),\ldots,\phi(t_n)$. The resulting kernel matrix is still SSS, but the SSS generators are defined in reverse order; see as remarked following \Cref{thm:sde-to-sss}.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
An SSS representation of $\mathbf{L}^{-1}$ can be computed in linear time using \Cref{alg:explicit:inverse}; the derivation and algorithm are provided in \Cref{app:additional:algorithms}. When $\mathbf{C}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{C}_n$ are square and nonsingular, the inverse of $\mathbf{L}$ is block bidiagonal, and $\mathbf{K}^{-1}$ is therefore block tridiagonal. This is shown in \Cref{app:block:tridiagonal}.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
An alternative to maximum likelihood estimation for hyperparameter selection is generalized cross validation (GCV) \cite{GHW:79}, which does not require a probabilistic noise model. As shown in \Cref{app:gcv}, the GCV score and its gradient can likewise be evaluated in linear time using the SSS representation of $\mathbf{K}+\bm{\Sigma}$.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
For LTI-SDE-induced kernels, the structure of $\mathbf{L}$ highlights the correspondence between $\mathbf{K}$ and the discrete-time model as
	\begin{align*}
		\mathbf{K} = \mathbf{L}\mathbf{L}^\top = \mathbf{C}(\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{N}^p\mathbf{T})^{-1}(\mathbf{P}-\bm{\Psi})(\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{N}^p\mathbf{T})^{-\top}\mathbf{C}^\top.
	\end{align*}
	In other words, we can view $\mathbf{K}$ as the covariance matrix for the output $\mathbf{y}_k = \mathbf{C}_k\mathbf{x}_k$ of a discrete process $\mathbf{x}_{k+1} = \mathbf{T}_k\mathbf{x}_k + \bm{\varepsilon}_k$ with $\bm{\varepsilon}_k \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{P}_k - \bm{\Psi}_k)$.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
